title: Home Electrification: There's not a lot to do, and it doesn't have to be hard (Part 1)
summary: Technology Connections on electrifying a typical US home: smart load-managing panels can avoid service upgrades, heat pumps replace furnaces, and backup heat strips rarely run.

assertions.quote: they can eliminate the expense of a service upgrade

verdicts.note: Load calculations and power-limiting devices often avoid upgrades, but some homes still need them and code acceptance varies.
Whether existing dwellings can fully electrify without upgrading service panels is called an open question under ongoing research.

assertions.quote: Except, uh, they do. Almost always.
spend 3 kW of power running the pump and get 9 or even 12 kW of heat energy out of it
why spend the $50 on a reversing valve when gas is cheap?
Heat pumps that work effectively below -10°F are just around the corner
heat strips are rarely needed when you have a heat pump

verdicts.note: True in mild climates and with cold-climate units sized to the load; in cold climates with standard units backup heat runs a noticeable share of hours.
Auxiliary resistance energy exceeded 40% of compressor heating energy at 5 of 11 all-electric sites and exceeded it at 2; every heat pump ran its auxiliary heater during or after defrost.

Auxiliary heat was a small fraction of output overall and near zero in mild weather, but it appeared from about 30-35 F, made up a median 11% of heating energy at 5 F and ran 25% of the time at -10 to 0 F.

assertions.quote: More insulation and better windows and doors will go hand-in-hand with building electrification
find out just how oversized your heating system is, which around here they almost always seem to be by a factor of 2
I’m not going to go into operating cost comparisons here as that’s a very local consideration
There are heat pumps which are designed to replace boilers, but they’ll be a bit more work

verdicts.note: Hydronic systems need air-to-water units or new distribution and often larger emitters, raising cost and complexity.
